report.summary: One failure, and it is a real product bug: the book validator only rejects an empty title, so a whitespace-only title such as "   " is accepted and returns 201 instead of 422. Fix app/main.py:75 to check `book.title.strip()` (matching the author check on line 77), then rerun the blank-title case along with the other validation cases.

causes.title: Whitespace-only book title is accepted by the API
causes.explanation: validate_book() tests `if not book.title`, which is only true for an empty string. A title of three spaces is truthy, so validation passes and the book is inserted, returning 201 Created. The author check on the next line uses `book.author.strip()`, so the title and author rules are inconsistent. The behaviour is deterministic and the test's expectation (422 with 'Title must not be blank') matches the intended rule, so the test is right to fail. The same validate_book() is used on create (line 154) and update (line 212), so both endpoints accept blank titles.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:63-66: test_invalid_book_is_rejected[blank-title] posts {"title": "   ", "author": "A"} and asserts status 422; failure is 'assert 201 == 422'.
app/main.py:75-76: `if not book.title:` / `raise HTTPException(422, "Title must not be blank")` - a title of "   " is truthy and is not rejected.
app/main.py:77: `if not book.author.strip():` - the author check strips whitespace, showing the intended behaviour for blank values.
app/main.py:154 and 212: validate_book(book) is called from the create and update paths, so the bug affects both.
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py validate_book(), change line 75 to `if not book.title.strip():`. Consider also stripping the stored value or adding a test for PUT with a whitespace-only title, since update (line 212) shares the validator. Then rerun tests/api/test_books_api.py.
